## Engineering Task Shape Analysis — `3b1b/manim` at `a31c4ae` (pre_2023_context stratum)

> Note: `compare_revisions` of `6199a00...a31c4ae` returns zero diff — the cutoff commit and HEAD are identical, so this analysis is code-structure-driven rather than delta-driven. Task shapes are inferred from internal structural signals: naming patterns, comments, cross-file dependencies, admitted incompleteness, and borrowed code attribution.

---

### 1. Architectural Scaffolding (dominant shape)

The entire `manimlib/` package represents a wholesale architectural rewrite. The original 3b1b/manim used Cairo/FFmpeg pipelines with a CPU-side renderer; this codebase has been rebuilt around a **GPU-first, OpenGL/ModernGL shader pipeline**.

Key evidence:

- [`Mobject`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/mobject.py?L58-111) carries `shader_folder`, `shader_dtype`, and `render_primitive` as class-level attributes, making the shader contract part of the object identity, not a rendering detail.
- [`ShaderWrapper`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/shader_wrapper.py?L29-158) is a standalone program-management layer that batches, hashes, and combines vertex data, with `#INSERT` preprocessing for GLSL code sharing ([L187-193](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/shader_wrapper.py?L187-193)).
- [`VMobject`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/types/vectorized_mobject.py?L50-66) declares separate `stroke_shader_folder` and `fill_shader_folder`, indicating two independent GPU render passes per vector object.
- [`CameraFrame`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/camera/camera.py?L31-67) is itself a `Mobject` carrying quaternion orientation as a uniform (`Rotation.identity().as_quat()`), replacing what was formerly a plain camera dict — a significant model change.
- The [`Surface`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/types/surface.py?L24-60), [`DotCloud`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/types/dot_cloud.py?L24-60), and shader directories (`quadratic_bezier_fill/`, `quadratic_bezier_stroke/`, `true_dot/`, `surface/`, `mandelbrot_fractal/`, `newton_fractal/`) confirm a multi-backend GPU surface system.
- [`Window`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/window.py?L18-48) wraps `moderngl_window`'s `PygletWindow`, a different windowing stack from the old PIL-to-file approach.

**Classification: architectural scaffolding** — the whole package is the scaffold; individual subsystems below subdivide further.

---

### 2. Feature — Interactive / Live Scene Editing

[`InteractiveScene`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/interactive_scene.py?L48-80) adds a fully novel capability absent from the original: a WYSIWYG editing mode with:
- Ctrl-drag selection, grab/resize/recolor gestures (`SELECT_KEY`, `GRAB_KEY`, `RESIZE_KEY`, `COLOR_KEY`).
- Clipboard-based paste of `Tex`, `Text`, or copied mobjects.
- Undo/redo via `SceneState` snapshots (referenced via `Scene.save_state`/`undo`/`redo` at [scene.py L688-699](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L688-699)).

The file opens with the comment _"a lot of the functionality here is still buggy and very much a work in progress"_ ([L45](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/interactive_scene.py?L45)), which marks this as an **in-progress feature**, not yet stabilized.

**Classification: feature** (live interactive editing subsystem; admitted WIP)

---

### 3. Feature — IPython Embed Shell

[`Scene.embed`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L193-284) provides a REPL-in-scene capability: an `InteractiveShellEmbed` session that keeps the render window live during IPython execution. Notable implementation choices:
- A custom `pt_inputhooks` hook ([L228-236](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L228-236)) prevents the event loop from blocking on input.
- A hack to copy locals into globals to fix lambda scoping in IPython ([L239-247](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L239-247)) — self-described as "admittedly sketchy".
- Post-cell hook refreshes static mobjects and saves scene state ([L250-256](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L250-256)).
- Error feedback via a red border flash + optional audio bell ([L259-266](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L259-266)).

**Classification: feature** (developer-experience tooling embedded in the animation runtime)

---

### 4. Feature — `_AnimationBuilder` / `.animate` Property

[`Mobject.animate`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/mobject.py?L161-164) returns an `_AnimationBuilder`. The inline comment reads _"Borrowed from https://github.com/ManimCommunity/manim/"_, making this an explicit cross-fork port.

**Classification: feature** (fluent animation API; acknowledged upstream borrow)

---

### 5. Feature — Boolean Geometry Operations

[`manimlib/mobject/boolean_ops.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/boolean_ops.py) provides `Union`, and implicitly `Intersection`/`Difference` via `skia-pathops`. The file comment also attributes the approach to ManimCommunity ([L10](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/boolean_ops.py?L10)).

**Classification: feature** (new capability; cross-fork attribution noted)

---

### 6. Feature — `StringMobject` / `MarkupText` Substring Isolation

[`StringMobject`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/svg/string_mobject.py?L25-79) is an abstract base providing substring-indexed submobject selection for `Tex` and `MarkupText`. It uses a "labelled SVG" trick — rendering a second SVG with injected color commands — to associate submobjects with source substrings. [`MarkupText`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/svg/text_mobject.py?L52-71) adds Pango/manimpango font rendering.

This replaces the older `old_tex_mobject.py` (`SingleStringTex`), which is retained as a compatibility shim.

**Classification: feature** (substring-aware text rendering; `old_tex_mobject.py` is residual compatibility, see §9)

---

### 7. Feature — Presenter Mode

[`Scene.__init__`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L77) accepts `presenter_mode`; `Scene.wait` honors it by calling `hold_loop()` ([L629-632](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L629-632)) instead of advancing time. CLI flag `-p`/`--presenter_mode` wires it to argparse ([config.py L78-80](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/config.py?L78-80)).

**Classification: feature** (slide-deck style playback control)

---

### 8. Feature — `TransformMatchingParts`

[`TransformMatchingParts`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/animation/transform_matching_parts.py?L25-60) pairs submobjects by shape identity using `has_same_shape_as` and `linear_sum_assignment` (scipy). This is a distinct new animation type that did not exist in the original Cairo-based manim.

**Classification: feature** (shape-matched morph animation)

---

### 9. Documentation / Configuration

- [`manimlib/default_config.yml`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/default_config.yml) and [`manimlib/tex_templates.yml`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/tex_templates.yml) are pure configuration.
- [`manimlib/typing.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/typing.py) is documentation-via-types: all definitions are under `TYPE_CHECKING`, making them zero-runtime annotation aliases. The file's own comment states: _"the names are here primarily to enhance readibility and allow for some stronger type checking if numpy has stronger typing in the future"_ ([L28-29](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/typing.py?L28-29)).
- [`pyproject.toml`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/pyproject.toml) is minimal (`requires = ["setuptools", "wheel"]`) — boilerplate package configuration.
- [`requirements.txt`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/requirements.txt) lists 24 runtime dependencies; notably `moderngl`, `moderngl_window`, `manimpango`, `skia-pathops`, `svgelements` — all dependencies not present in the legacy codebase.

**Classification: documentation/configuration** (typing.py, yml files); **boilerplate** (pyproject.toml, setup.cfg/setup.py)

---

### 10. Dependency Migration (inferred, ambiguous)

The `requirements.txt` dependency set (`moderngl`, `moderngl_window`, `pyglet` via `mglw`, `manimpango`, `skia-pathops`, `scipy`, `svgelements`) represents a categorical switch from the previous Cairo + FFmpeg + LaTeX-only stack. These are not additive dependencies; they replace the rendering substrate.

There is no test suite present in the repository at this revision (no `tests/` directory, no `pytest` in requirements), so **test generation** and **localized bug fix** shapes are not evidenced by any files.

**Classification: dependency migration** — _ambiguous in isolation_; migration is inseparable from the architectural scaffolding (§1) because the new GPU subsystem mandated the new dependencies, not vice versa. It does not stand alone as a separate task.

---

### 11. Localized Bug Fix — Evidenced Only by Comments (low confidence)

The codebase contains several comments that signal known bugs or workarounds rather than resolved fixes:

- Window position double-assignment (`self.position = initial_position` set twice, [window.py L47-48](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/window.py?L47-48)): _"doing it twice seems to make it work. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯"_ — an unresolved platform bug, not a fix.
- FPS hardcode in scene init ([scene.py L102](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L102)): _"Where's that 30 from?"_ — acknowledged incorrectness.
- `Scene.has_time_based_updaters` calls `self.mobjects()` as a function ([scene.py L335](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/scene/scene.py?L335)) which would raise `TypeError` at runtime — an unfixed bug present in the snapshot.

These are **open bugs**, not resolved ones. No localized bug-fix task shape is evidenced.

---

### 12. Refactor — `copy()` / Serialization Overhaul

[`Mobject.copy`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/mobject.py?L563-603) does not simply call `deepcopy`; it manually copies numpy arrays, rebuilds the `parents`/`family` graph, and remaps named family-member attributes. A `stash_mobject_pointers` decorator ([L532-546](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/mobject.py?L532-546)) temporarily nulls graph pointers for serialization.

This is a performance-motivated refactor of object copying within the new data model (numpy-backed `data` dict replacing per-attribute numpy fields).

**Classification: refactor** (copying/serialization model within the new architecture)

---

### 13. Cleanup — `old_tex_mobject.py`

[`manimlib/mobject/svg/old_tex_mobject.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/-/blob/manimlib/mobject/svg/old_tex_mobject.py) exists alongside the new `tex_mobject.py` and `string_mobject.py`. The filename prefix `old_` signals it is retained for backward compatibility with scenes that import `SingleStringTex` or similar names directly, but it is not the canonical path. Its presence is cleanup-deferred residue.

**Classification: cleanup** (deferred; the file is legacy retention, not yet removed)

## Taxonomy Refinement Proposal

The existing eight categories handle this codebase well with one gap worth noting:

> **"architectural scaffolding" conflates two distinguishable shapes**: (a) *greenfield system construction* (new GPU pipeline, new object model, new windowing) and (b) *cross-fork feature porting* (`.animate`, boolean ops, `StringMobject`). The latter carries explicit attribution comments and a known upstream (ManimCommunity). Proposed addition: **`upstream-port`** — a task that deliberately transplants a feature from a forked or related project, distinct from independent feature work because the design decisions are inherited rather than originated. This would cleanly separate `.animate` and `boolean_ops.py` from the original architectural work without distorting the other categories.

The existing eight categories handle this codebase well with one gap worth noting:
